sections.title: Column crack vs paint crack — know the difference
sections.body: A fine crack in plaster between two rooms is usually cosmetic — the brick partition carries no load. A crack that follows a column line, runs diagonally across a wall-ceiling joint, or widens after each tremor is structural. If you can fit a coin into the crack and it goes deep, or if the crack reappears after repainting, call us.

sections.title: Even new flats in Guwahati aren't automatically safe
sections.body: Building codes exist — but enforcement and construction quality vary. Many flats built in the last 10 years have the same hidden problems: honeycombed concrete, insufficient steel, and rushed curing. A 'new' tag on a property listing doesn't mean earthquake-safe. A building strength test takes a few hours and tells you the truth.

sections.title: What happens in the next tremor — treated vs untreated
sections.body: An untreated home with a cracked column: the tremor shakes the building, stress concentrates at the crack, the column shears, upper floors lose support. A retrofitted home: the same tremor is absorbed by strengthened columns — cracks may not grow, floors stay supported.

sections.title: How RCC strength drops over time
sections.body: Concrete does not stay at day-one strength forever. Carbonation front moves inward and reduces alkalinity that protects steel. Cover spalls, chlorides from poor mix or leaks reach rebar, and corrosion expands. IS 456 expects durability planning — not build-and-forget. A 25-year column in Guwahati monsoon can test 30–40% below original design assumptions if never maintained.

sections.title: Who should get tested?
bullets: Anyone buying a resale flat or house in Guwahati
Owners of buildings 10+ years old — especially pre-2010 construction
Flats where cracks appeared after recent tremors
Housing societies planning major renovation or additional floors
Landlords who want to protect tenants and avoid liability

sections.title: What you'll receive
sections.body: A clear report in plain language — not a 50-page engineering document. We mark which columns passed, which need attention, and what it will cost to fix. You decide whether to proceed with purchase, negotiate price, or walk away.

sections.title: How RCC strength decreases with age
sections.body: Carbonation, chloride ingress, and cover loss reduce effective strength over decades — often with no visible warning until spalling or a tremor widens cracks. Rebound hammer and UPV show what paint hides. A building that 'looks fine' at 20 years may have columns below design capacity.

sections.title: When to retest — every 3 to 5 years
sections.body: IS 456 and good international practice treat structural health as ongoing. After major tremors, visible new cracks, or completed retrofit work, retest sooner. For older occupied buildings, a 3–5 year NDT cycle catches corrosion and strength loss before emergency repair.

sections.title: Other states already mandate audits
sections.body: Maharashtra requires structural audits for certain ageing and dilapidated buildings. Delhi authorities have pushed periodic safety inspections on old structures. Kerala intensified assessments after flood damage. Assam has not yet mandated the same — but owners who wait for law often pay emergency prices after failure.

sections.title: The Guwahati monsoon trap
sections.body: From May to September, Guwahati gets heavy rain almost daily. Flat terraces, shared apartment roofs, and old drainage systems can't cope. If your upstairs neighbour's terrace isn't waterproofed, your ceiling pays the price. If your own terrace has cracks, your columns absorb the water.

sections.title: Signs you need waterproofing now
bullets: Yellow-brown stains on ceiling or walls after rain
Peeling paint or bubbling plaster in bathroom or terrace-adjacent rooms
Musty smell that returns every monsoon
White powder (efflorescence) on ground-floor walls
Water dripping from terrace drain areas

sections.title: Diagnosis before coating
sections.body: We flood-test terraces, map moisture on ceilings, and check parapet and drain details before specifying membrane type. Coating over active cracks or ponding water fails within one season — diagnosis first saves repeat cost.

sections.title: When PU injection is the right call
sections.body: Active water through a crack or joint — basement during monsoon, terrace slab, expansion joint, pipe penetration. PU reacts with water and expands to seal. Dry structural cracks need epoxy, not PU alone.

sections.title: Monsoon urgency
sections.body: Active leaks accelerate steel corrosion inside slabs and columns. Every week water reaches reinforcement, rust expands, and repair scope grows. Emergency PU injection can run during rain; full waterproofing follows once the leak path is sealed.

sections.title: PU injection process
bullets: Locate leak path — not just visible drip point
Drill packers along crack or joint at set spacing
Inject hydrophilic or hydrophobic PU under pressure
Verify seal with water test
Finish surface and recommend permanent waterproofing where needed
